correctness.rationale: In the six-dimensional even-subsets/complement symplectic module, matchings give 105 distinct Lagrangians; all 15 Lagrangians through a specified two-subset class are accounted for by matchings containing that pair. The seven affine plane-partition classes close as the nonzero part of a Lagrangian and have zero pairings. Their partition families recover the affine structure: after choosing an origin, choose the side of each partition containing it and thereby recover all affine linear coordinates up to affine change. The 30 structures exhaust the complement of the matchings among 135 Lagrangians. For every partition, I independently inventoried elements of each S8 cycle type in AGL(3,2), used the centralizer/coset formula on powers, and inverted the fixed numbers; all 22 rows of orbit_profiles.json and the displayed profiles agree. The matching counts independently follow by viewing a matching as an involution without fixed points commuting with Frobenius: pair equal-length cycles with an arbitrary alignment, or exchange an even-length cycle with itself by a half-turn. At (1,7), the fixed cosets number 2 and the remaining 28 form four 7-cycles; no matching is fixed. An odd-order permutation cannot swap complementary subsets, and the only invariant even subsets here are empty and full. Thus there is no nonzero rational 2-torsion despite the two stable subgroup schemes. Direct FLINT factorization confirms x^7+x+1 is irreducible over F5 and its product with x is squarefree; the smooth degree-eight hyperelliptic model has genus three and these eight finite branch points. The zeta function follows from two degree-one and four degree-seven places.
residual_risks: This is rationality of subgroup schemes, not of all their points, nor an assertion about a Jacobian quotient over the ground field. Only branch types realized by the curve apply.
